chapter: Reflections on Paris guitarists and saxophonists
title: Melody Maker headline and the Hawkins-Carter jam at Aikian's club
summary: Butler tells how Coleman Hawkins disliked a Dutch headline about his fall, and of the Czech saxophonist Andre Aikian's club, where Benny Carter pulled out a tenor to irk Hawkins.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x:
And that's what was happening.

And -- oh, of course, me and Patterson, that was the golden days.

They had at one time the Melody Maker, which was an English newspaper of jazz. They says, the rise and fall of King Coleman Hawkins.

And Benny Carter -- Coleman Hawkins happened to be in town and Benny Carter showed Coleman Hawkins that caption, yeah, yeah.

Coleman looked -- because he couldn't read very -- he'd been in Harlem so long so he couldn't -- read Dutch -- and you see, Coleman Hawkins was the type of man you said, have you studied music, he said, I don't know nothing about music. And he plays the piano, he'd studied the cello and that horn and four hours every day he practiced three/and you'd go visit him while he was practising, he would put the horn away and say, 'Well, let's go across the street and have a drink' and he'd get you away from him.

That's the type of man -- I think that's why they called him the Hawk.

So, he looked at it and there was a man, a very handsome man his name was Andre Aikian. He was a man from Czechoslovakia, as I told you before, he could play.

Well, (inaudible) and the ladies were -- that was it. He would play that saxaphone and they loved him. He

was beautiful. He was handsome.

And he had a little club and he had a little poodle dog, you know, they called him Mimi. And little Mimi, when we got off, we went to (inaudible) place to meet our girlfriends, we'd meet each other.

There was another place we'd go is Budals, (phonetic). That was across the street from the post office. We would go there later anyway, see, we would go there later anyway.

So, Aikian's place was on, I think it was Rue -- well, I I said, Rue Perrier (phonetic) I know that -- and Rue Perrier is on that triangle there, coming out from Piqalle.

And all of us was there and Coleman Hawkins and Benny Carter pulled out the tenor saxophone and started to playing it, in order to irk Coleman Hawkins.

Now, Djangos and all the guitarists, all his cousins and things were there, they wasn't playing -- they was just -- and there was another fellow named Alx Combelle (phonetic) also a beautiful tenor saxophone player.

So, I think they got to playing 'Honeysuckle Rose' and Benny Carter, well, you know how Benny Carter -- he's the dean of the saxophone. He don't make no mistakes at all. Everything fits in just like a machine. Beautiful.
